evals.prompt: Design the instruction-file architecture for a repo used from Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and Gemini without duplicating the same workflow text.
evals.expected_output: A single root AGENTS.md with no CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md stubs, Gemini pointed at AGENTS.md through context.fileName, and domain detail kept in skills.
assertions: The response makes AGENTS.md the only instruction body
The response does not add a CLAUDE.md bridge by default and notes that one would stop Claude Code reading AGENTS.md
The response configures Gemini through context.fileName rather than a GEMINI.md body
The response distinguishes top-level instruction content from skill-level detail

evals.prompt: Review AGENTS.md after several new skills were added and tell me what should change.
evals.expected_output: A review that checks commands and workflow drift and size budgets, and does not add the new skills as a catalog because clients already list skill descriptions.
assertions: The response does not add a skill catalog to AGENTS.md
The response checks workflow or command drift
The response checks the file against the size budgets

evals.prompt: Our repo has a .claude/CLAUDE.md that just contains @../AGENTS.md. Should we keep it?
evals.expected_output: Guidance that deletes the stub because current Claude Code reads AGENTS.md natively, keeping it only for clients on versions before v2.1.277.
assertions: The response recommends deleting the stub by default
The response names the Claude Code version condition
The response does not suggest moving content into CLAUDE.md

evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md has 120 lines of its own rules and AGENTS.md has different ones. Clean this up.
evals.expected_output: Merge the CLAUDE.md body into AGENTS.md, resolve contradictions, then delete CLAUDE.md.
assertions: The response merges the CLAUDE.md content into AGENTS.md
The response resolves contradictions rather than keeping both
